content:
I would like to upgrade the simpVarHead linter from an environment linter to a syntax linter. My idea is to get a copy of the environment from before and after a given declaration. If there is a bad simp lemma in the latter and not in the former, then the linter should complain.

The issue is, I'm not sure how to get the two copies of the environment. Does anyone have advice?
Not an answer to your question about environments, but note that the simpVarHead linter is moving to core and will trigger the moment the simp attribute is added: lean4#13325.

Ah great, then I don't have to do anything!

My plan was also to extend the linter to give a warning when the head key is .other (currently it warns only on .star). This is because such lemmas also cause slowdowns (though not as much as .star lemmas). Could this also be added to core?
Sounds good to me! Thanks for bringing this up!

Re: the general question of how to get the environment before a command in a linter, it would be great to be able to capture parts of the environment before a command during linting, but as far as I know you'd need to hack around this with IO.Refs. :(

(Note: I asked a related question, initially restricted to declarations but mentioning this possibility, in #lean4 > Pre-RFC: show new decls to interactive linters, but it didn't pick up any traction. As an aside, I've found that the approach used by docs#Mathlib.Linter.getNamesFrom in mathlib for getting declarations is more efficient and reliable for getting declarations from the current command than traversing infotrees, though still worse than a core change would be; I've made it a bit more performant and better-suited to linting in batteries#1754. Maybe it would have applied here?)

One might expect that given some of the surrounding docstrings in CommandContextInfo, the env stored in the topmost command context in the infotrees could help us out here, but unfortunately that also seems not to be the case. :(

import Lean.Elab.Command

open Lean Meta Elab Command

def checkForFoo : Linter where
  name := `checkForFoo
  run _ := do
    let ts ← getInfoTrees
    if h : ts.size = 1 then
      let env ← match ts[0] with
        | .context (.commandCtx info) _ => pure info.env
        | _ => throwError "Infotree did not start with command context."
      logInfo
        m!"Found foo in current environment: {(← getEnv).contains `foo} (isInstance: {isInstanceCore (← getEnv) `foo})\n\
        Found foo in 'initial' infotree environment: {env.containsOnBranch `foo} (isInstance: {isInstanceCore env `foo})"
    else
      throwError "Found {ts.size} infotrees, expected 1"

run_cmd do
  lintersRef.modify fun linters => linters.filter (·.name != `checkForFoo)
  addLinter checkForFoo

/--
info: Found foo in current environment: true (isInstance: true)
Found foo in 'initial' infotree environment: true (isInstance: true)
-/
#guard_msgs in
public instance foo : Nonempty Bool := ⟨true⟩
I think that having a flag for linters that allows them to act before a declaration is elaborated would be great!

For instance, checking whether a set_option ... in flag is necessary, the easier approach would be to elaborate the ... part alone. But if that is a declaration, then you have to wrestle that the declaration already exists in the environment and elaboration will fail, independently of the option.

Just added the check for .other as well: lean4#13325
Nice! We could also consider warning on the pattern#[.forall, .star]. However, there is the lemma docs#IsEmpty.forall_iff which would get flagged by this.
